title: udp_rate_limiting plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `udp_rate_limiting` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component UdpRateLimitingConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

UdpRateLimitingConfig.description:
Configuration for the `udp_rate_limiting` plugin. Rate limits UDP
datagrams per resolved client IP using a fixed-window algorithm with
atomic counters. Excess datagrams are silently dropped (standard UDP
flood mitigation). By default (`direction: both`) client→backend and
backend→client datagrams share the same window per client IP; IPv6
clients are grouped by `ipv6_prefix`. A proxy- or proxy-group-scoped
attachment must reach only UDP/DTLS proxies (a TCP or HTTP-family
target is refused at admission). `datagrams_per_second`
and `bytes_per_second` are per-second rates; the effective per-window
cap is `rate × window_seconds`. `sync_mode` is parsed case-insensitively
(`LOCAL`, `Redis`); `redis` requires `redis_url`. Unknown top-level keys
are rejected by the runtime and by this schema. Counter storage supports
only local memory and Redis; database-backed counters are intentionally
unsupported. Residual admission rules this schema cannot express,
enforced by the constructor alone: the checked product of a configured
rate and `window_seconds` must fit in an unsigned 64-bit integer.

datagrams_per_second.description: Sustained datagram rate per second per client IP. The effective per-window cap is `datagrams_per_second × window_seconds`. With the default `direction: both`, client→backend and backend→client datagrams count against the same cap. At least one of `datagrams_per_second` or `bytes_per_second` is required.

bytes_per_second.description: Sustained payload-byte rate per second per client IP (sum of datagram payload sizes). The effective per-window cap is `bytes_per_second × window_seconds`. With the default `direction: both`, both directions count against the same cap. At least one of `datagrams_per_second` or `bytes_per_second` is required.

window_seconds.description: Window length in seconds. Defaults to 1 second. Capped at 2678400 (31 days) so the derived Redis TTL (`window_seconds + 1`) and activity-retention horizon (`window_seconds × 2`) cannot wrap. The effective per-window cap is `datagrams_per_second × window_seconds` (and similarly for bytes).

ipv6_prefix.description: IPv6 prefix length used to group client addresses into one budget (for example 56 or 48 to stop rotation across a delegated prefix). IPv4 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 clients remain host-specific.

direction.description: Which datagrams are counted and limited. `both` (default) charges client→backend and backend→client datagrams to one combined budget; `client_to_backend` or `backend_to_client` limits only that direction and neither counts nor drops the other.

sync_mode.description: Datagram/byte counter storage: 'local' (in-memory) or 'redis' (centralized), parsed case-insensitively. `redis` additionally requires `redis_url`. Database-backed counters are unsupported.

redis_url.description: Redis connection URL (e.g., redis://host:6379/0), required with sync_mode=redis. The database selector is a canonical decimal integer from 0 through 2147483647, without signs, zero-padding, or extra slashes. An absent path or bare slash selects database 0. Ferrum uses the portable signed-32-bit bound; redis-rs represents indexes as i64. The server separately checks its configured databases on SELECT. TCP port range is constructor-validated. URL fragments are forbidden; TLS skip-verify is only FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_tls.description: Enable TLS for the Redis connection. CA verification uses gateway-level FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; skip-verify uses FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY.

redis_key_prefix.description: Key prefix for all Redis keys. Defaults to `{FERRUM_NAMESPACE}:{plugin_name}:{plugin-config-id}` so two independent policies of this plugin type in one namespace do not share counters. Must be non-empty when set; setting it explicitly is the documented opt-in for a deliberately shared budget: every instance configured with the same prefix increments and rejects against the same counters.

redis_pool_size.description: Number of multiplexed Redis connections. Must be between 1 and 128.

redis_failure_policy.description: Behavior when the centralized Redis store cannot be consulted: an outage, an egress/DNS screen failure, or an endpoint rejected as an unsupported topology (Redis Cluster is not supported). fail_closed drops the datagram; local_fallback explicitly opts into per-process budgets, which enforce the configured limit once per gateway process. Only meaningful with sync_mode=redis, but validated in either mode.

redis_connect_timeout_seconds.description: Redis connection timeout in seconds. Must be a positive unsigned 64-bit integer.

redis_health_check_interval_seconds.description: Health check ping interval when Redis is unavailable. Must be a positive unsigned 64-bit integer.
